Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of Australia. It seems quite chilly out there as David Warner has his hands firmly in his pockets with the hand-warmers and the sweater vests are on. It will be the pairing of Brandon King and Johnson Charles to open the innings for West Indies. It will be Jason Behrendorff to start proceedings with the ball here. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, 214 is a mammoth score to chase on any ground but West Indies do have the firepower. It will all depend on whether they can consistently take on the Aussie attack and come out on top. Australia will certainly feel confident of defending this total but you never know. Do join us in a bit for the exciting run chase.

On the other hand, West Indies were very shoddy with the ball at the start and Akeal Hosein had a day to forget as he looked to bowl seam-up instead of trying to grip the ball and David Warner punished him. Alzarri Joseph bowled well but was unlucky throughout and it was Jason Holder who broke the frustrating opening stand. The likes of Joseph, Romario Shepherd and Andre Russell all managed to capitalize a bit in the second half of the game and got timely wickets. However, the boundaries started to flow again towards the death but Russell bowled a brilliant final over, picking up two wickets and almost finished on a high as he did concede a boundary on the very final delivery.

Now that was some batting performance from Australia and they have brought up the equal highest T20I total on this ground by posting 213 runs on the board. The Australian innings started off with a bang as David Warner looked like his devastating best and took on the Windies bowlers inside the Powerplay for plenty of runs. Josh Inglis gave him ample support and played his shots too but did get out inside the first 10 overs. They were 110/1 at the halfway stage but then the wickets started to fall at regular intervals and they lost their way a bit in the next 6 overs. Warner got out on 70 quick runs but at the death, the pair of Matthew Wade and Tim David found the fence with regularity and the latter finished unbeaten on 37 off just 17 balls that took Australia to over 210 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Skillful from Josh Inglis and for a moment he looked gone for all money. Slower one at just 116 clicks and on yorker length at the off stump, Inglis looks for the reverse-lap and seems to be beaten by the lack pace but does well in the end to split the keeper and short fine leg for a boundary.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts off with a short ball outside off, this is dug into the pitch and Josh Inglis fails to put it away.

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! Slower bumper from Alzarri Joseph, well-directed as well and Josh Inglis is beaten. The ball goes off Inglis' back and onto the off side as the batters scamper through for a leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BOOM! Full and in the slot, angling into the swinging arc as well. David Warner sits down and slog-sweeps it a long way over deep mid-wicket for the first maximum of the innings and Australia are off to a flier here.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to begin. The umpires make their way out to the middle followed by the West Indies fielder. David Warner and Josh Inglis are the opening batters for Australia. Akeal Hosein has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. David Warner becomes the first Aussie and the third player in the world to play 100 T201 games. Truly a legend of the game! Let's go...

West Indies (Playing XI) - Brandon King, Johnson Charles, Nicholas Pooran (WK), Shai Hope, Rovman Powell (C), Sherfane Rutherford, Andre Russell, Jason Holder, Romario Shepherd, Akeal Hosein, Alzarri Joseph.
Australia (Playing XI) - Josh Inglis, David Warner, Mitchell Marsh (C), Glenn Maxwell, Marcus Stoinis, Tim David, Matthew Wade (WK), Sean Abbott, Adam Zampa, Jason Behrendorff, Josh Hazlewood.
TOSS - West Indies win the toss and they will BOWL first.

West Indies on the other hand will be looking to forget the ODI series and do their best to prepare for a home T20I World Cup in a few months time by putting on a good performance against a strong side like Australia. Skipper, Rovman Powell will be the one to keep an eye on along with Nicholas Pooran as the pair can take the game away from the opposition but they do also have plenty of firepower with the bat, both at the top and in the middle order. Akeal Hosein and Gudakesh Motie, the two spinners have been consistent in recent times but it is the pace attack that looks undercooked and we might see Andre Russell bowl his full quota. Can the Windies flex their muscle and outpower the Aussies? Or will the home side once again prove to be clinical? We shall find out. Toss and team news in a bit.

Australia comes into this contest on the back of a resounding 3-0 win in the ODI series against the same opposition but the side that they will face now will be pretty different than the one in the ODIs. Also, the likes of Steven Smith and Travis Head have been rested for this series. Mitchell Marsh will be leading the side and will be looking to get into his groove right away. The middle order looks stacked and with the addition of Aaron Hardie in the squad, the Aussies have no shortage of all-rounders in the team as well but will need to find the right balance.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the 1st T20I between Australia and West Indies from the Blundstone Arena in Hobart. Two sides that are filled with entertaining individuals and a lot of muscle power but only one can come out on top as both sides look to prepare for the T20 World Cup later in the year.
